newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah lower, adjusted to fixing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah lower, adjusted to fixing.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was lower against the dollar in slow late trading on Tuesday following a small adjustment of the central bank's fixing, dealers said.
One Japanese bank dealer said there were no fresh leads in the afternoon, keeping the market trading in a narrow-range, with some weakening of the rupiah seen after the fixing.
The central bank raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,334/2,526 and the conversion rate to 2,334/2,382.
"It's not a surprise because people have widely anticipated this since the morning," the dealer said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,335.00/35.25 at 0845 GMT against an opening of 2,334.60/35.10. Tomorrow and today closed at 2,334.5/35.0 and 2,334.25/34.75, respectively.
"Sentiment on the rupiah remains unchanged," he said.

Dealers said operators seemed to shrug off the anniversary of Santa Cruz massacre in East Timor in 1991. Students protested in front of the University of East Timor on Tuesday morning to mark the killing of at least 50 demonstrators in the capital Dili.
Dealers said swap rates were generally soft on ample supply of the rupiah in the money market.
Both short and long-term rates were lower in slow trade.
Overnight swap was at 0.15/0.25 and tom/next at 0.20/0.25.
One-month swap edged down to 15.0/15.2 from 15.50/16.25, two to 30.5/31.5 from 31.0/32.0, three to 47.0/48.5 from 47.5/48.5 and six to 92.25/94.00 from 94.0/94.5 points.
"It's a good time to buy swap at present because it seems to have bottomed out. I think the rates may recover when Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) makes its debut," one said.
BNI will be listed on November 25.
